result:
Implemented the cap in `crates/ucal/src/clock.rs`: `Session::reading` now limits how far a single reading may advance ahead of the monotonic projection (`anchor + monotonic_elapsed`) to `MAX_ADVANCE_NANOS` (1 second) per call. A wall-clock jump larger than that is deferred rather than refused — subsequent readings keep closing the gap as real time passes, since the monotonic branch advances continuously regardless of how often `reading()` is polled. Elapsed real time itself (wall and monotonic agreeing) is never capped, only genuine forward discontinuities are.

Updated/added tests in `clock.rs` cover: a forward step under the cap being accepted in full, a large jump being capped and then caught up over subsequent readings, and honest elapsed time never being throttled. Both `cargo test -q -p ucal --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -q -p xtask --no-fail-fast` pass. No commit was made, per instructions.
